 Judgment
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 24-05-2022 at about 6-00 p.m. the petitioner was traveling as a pillion rider in a Hero Splendor bearing Reg.No.AP-03/BS-6225 along with his son V. Dharani Prasad on Chennai -Bangalore High way, Chittoor and when he reached near Muttarapalli bus stop, Yadamari, at that time driver of Eicher goods vehicle bearing Reg.NoKA-08/8865 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the petitioner's motor cycle from behind, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Govt.,
Hospital, Chittoor wherein first aid treatment was given and then he was shifted to Sankalpa Super Specialty Hospital, Tirupathi wherein admitted as an inpatient from 20-05-2022 to 30-05-2022 and undergone surgery and discharged with the advice to come for follow up treatment.
The petitioner is still under treatment.
2(a). Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
He was aged about 74 years.
He was Agriculturist by profession and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the permanent disability, he is not in a position to do the said work.
He has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability & loss of income.
3. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1/
the R.C. owner of Eicher goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA- 08/8865 remained absent and hence he was placed exparte.

4. Respondent no.2/the insurer of Eicher goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-08/8865 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
The respondent no.2 has contended that the driver of the insured vehicle was not holding driving license, Permit and F.C. as on the date of accident.
It is further contended that the insured vehicle was not at all involved in the accident.
The petitioner in collision with the jurisdictional police have created false record and lodged false complaint, to get compensation.

The respondent no.2 has contended that the alleged accident has Subramanyam.V vs Balakrishna on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57425363/
2 occurred due to the negligent act on the part of the petitioner.
There was no negligence on the part of the driver of the insured vehicle.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in the RTA alleged to have occurred on 24-05-2022 at about 6-00 p.m., at Muttarapalli bus stop,
Yadamari, Chennai - Bangalore High way, Chittoor, due to rash and negligence driving of the driver of Eicher goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-08-8865?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
3.

What Order or Award?
6.
The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and examined one witness as P.W.2 and marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P16 and Ex.P19 to Ex.P24.
During the cross examination of RW.1, the learned counsel for the petitioner confronted documents and got marked at Ex.P17 and Ex.P18.

The respondent no.2 got examined Casualty medical Officer, Chittoor Govt., Hospital, Chittoor by name Dr.Vikas Reddy as Rw.1 and got marked one document as Ex.R1.
7.
Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and respondent no.2 and perused the entire materials placed on record.

8. My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;

REASONS 9. Issue No.1 : - In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of Eicher goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-08/8865, the P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 24-05-2022 at about 6-00 p.m. when the petitioner was traveling as a pillion rider in Hero Splendor bearing Reg.No.AP-03/BS-6225 along with his son V. Dharani Prasad on Chennai -Bangalore High way, Chittoor and when he reached near Muttarapalli bus stop,
Yadamari

, at that time the driver of Eicher goods vehicle bearing Reg.NoKA-08/8865 (herein after called the offending vehicle) drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the petitioner's motor cycle from behind, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.

Subramanyam.V vs Balakrishna on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57425363/
3 10.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle,
P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 6 which are the police records such as FIR with complaint, Case diary, Sketch with translated copy, Accident Information report, Wound certificate and Charge sheet etc.,
11.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Dharani Prasad, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.100/2022 of Yadamari Police Station, Chittoor Dist., for the offence punishable under section 337 of IPC.

The investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 338 IPC Sec.134(A), 134(B) of M.V. Act.
12.

The respondent got examined one witness Dr.Vikas Reddy, the Causality Medical Officer of Chittoor Govt., Hospital, Chittoor as RW.1 and got marked one document as Ex.R1.
13.
So far as the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is concerned, admittedly the respondent no.1 who is the owner of offending vehicle has not contested the petition.
It is true that there is delay of 9 days in lodging the complaint as accident has occurred on 24-05-2022 at about 6-00 pm., and complaint came to be lodged on 31-01-2022.
If the medical records are perused, the petitioner was hospitalized for a long period in different hospitals, for different periods.
He has sustained grievous injuries.
If Ex.P17 is perused, it clearly reveals that soon after the accident the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Andra Pradesh, Chittor and history of Road Traffic Accident.
The wound certificate also discloses the said fact.
Hence, merely because there is delay of 8 days in lodging the complaint the court cannot raise doubt regarding the petitioner sustained injuries due to the Road Traffic Accident.
14. So far as the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is concerned, as per the case of petitioner, he was traveling in the motorcycle as pillion rider of which his son was the rider.

In the written statement the respondent no.2 has contended that at the time of accident the petitioner himself was riding the motorcycle and because of his rash and negligent riding, this mishap has occurred.
But there is no material to substantiate the said defence taken by the respondent no.2.
They have not even examined the driver of offending vehicle to prove that at the time of accident petitioner himself was riding the motorcycle.
15. As per the case of petitioner, the offending vehicle which came from the same direction in which the petitioner was proceeding hit to the vehicle of the petitioner on its rear side.
All the police records discloses the said fact.

At the cost of repetition the respondents have not examined the driver of the offending vehicle to prove that the accident in question has occurred in the manner other than the one contended by the petitioner.
Hence, there is every reason to believe that the offending vehicle which came from behind the vehicle of the petitioner hit to the motorcycle on its rear side.
Had the driver of the offending vehicle maintained minimum distance between the two vehicle this accident would not have occurred.
Hence, without discussing much on this point this court holds issue no.1 in the affirmative.

Subramanyam.V vs Balakrishna on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57425363/
4 16.
Issue No.2:-
The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate and Discharge summaries which are at Ex.P5, Ex.P10 and Ex.P19.
On going through the medical documents, it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment at Andhra Pradesh Vaidya Vidhana Parishad on 24-05- 2022.

Then he was admitted as inpatient from 25-05- 2022 to 30-05-2022 at Sankalpa Hospital,
Tirupati.
Thereafter, the petitioner was admitted at DBR & SK Super Speciality Hospital Tirupati on two occasions i.e., from 21-09-2022 to 24-09-2022 and 15-11-2022 and 16- 11-2022.
Then the petitioner has admitted as inpatient at Aster Narayanadri Hospital from 09-11-2024 to 13-11- 2024.
In all for a period of 18 days he has taken treatment.
As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained two injuries which are grievous in nature.
17. Dr. S.A. Somashekara, the Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru is examined as Pw2 and through him Out patient record and X-ray are got marked as Ex.P.15 and Ex.P16.
P.W.2 has deposed that he examined the petitioner on 27-08-2024 clinically, radiologically for disability assessment.
PW.2 further deposed that petitioner has sustained permanent physical disability of right lower limb at 68% and whole body disability at 34%.
PW.2 further deposed that the petitioner needs revision surgery for achieving union which would cost around Rs.1,00,000/- in Private set up.
18. If the evidence of PW.2 is perused, he is not a treated doctor.
As per the evidence of PW.2, the petitioner has sustained three fracture injuries on his right leg of which two fractures are united.

As per the own evidence of PW.2 the petitioner had fracture injury sustained earlier to the accident and the said old fracture injury is mal united and the out plant fixed to the injured organ of the petitioner is removed.
According to the PW.2 the petitioner is suffering from Arthritis and admitted that as age passes person suffers from Arthritis.
It is deposed by PW.2 that he has advised the petitioner either to undergo revision surgery or amputation.
But if the discharge summary and other medical records are perused, it was not suggested for amputation of right leg of the petitioner.
Though PW.2 has assessed the disability of petitioner on right lower limb at 68% but he has assessed the disability on whole body at 34%.

As per judgment reported in 2014 (4) Kar.L.J 157 Vijaya Kumar Alias Babu Rao Vs The Secretary, Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee Balki,
Taluk the normal rule would be disability in the lower limb would be 1/3rd of the particular limb.

entities.text:
2014 (4) Kar.L.J 157 Vijaya Kumar Alias Babu Rao Vs The Secretary, Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee Balki,
Taluk
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence if the disability on particular limb is 68% then on whole body the disability would have to be 22%.
It is true that on the date of recording the evidence of PW.1 he has come to the court in a wheel chair as he was not in a position to walk.
But if the very evidence of the PW.2 is perused, the petitioner had old fracture injury which is mal-united.
Further the petitioner has Arthritis problem and he is aged about 74 years.
Hence, because of this problems so also due to the injury sustained in the accident the petitioner may not be able to walk independently.

Hence, this court by relying upon the evidence of PW.2 arrives at the conclusion that the petitioner has suffered disability of 20%
instead of 22% or 34% has assessed by PW.2.
19. Considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken, this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
20. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained two grievous injuries.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and the time taken for Subramanyam.V vs Balakrishna on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57425363/
5 treatment and sufferings during the treatment, it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.70,000/- towards pain and suffering.

21. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner are concerned, he has produced Ex.P11- medical bills for Rs.3,83,024/-, which includes ambulance bill of Rs.2,10,000/- but if the ambulance bills produced by the petitioner is carefully perused, they appears to be not genuine document for the reason that the ambulance bills produced by the petitioner is dated 25-05-2022,
09- 06-2022, 15-11-2022, 21-09-2022, 16-11-2022, 08-09- 2022, 22-09-2022, 24-09-2022,
14-11-2022.
Though the said ambulance bills are of different dates but the serial number of the ambulance bills are Sl No.19 to 29.

When petitioner stated to have shifted to hospital in the alleged ambulance in a gap of nearly 6 years on different dates there is no possibility of issuing ambulances bills having continues serial numbers.
It appears that the said ambulance bills are issued on the same date for the purpose of producing before the court.
Hence, the ambulance bills produced by the petitioner cannot be relied upon.
The petitioner has produced further medical bills as per Ex.P 22 for Rs. Rs.49,587/-.
Inpatient final bill for Rs.28,985.19/- as per Ex.P24.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses to the tune of Rs.2,51,596/-.
22.
It is stated that petitioner was aged about 74 years and he was Agriculturist by profession and earning sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
But to substantiate the said contention petitioner has not produced any materials.

Hence this court considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence of the petitioner takes the income of the petitioner at Rs.15,500/- p.m.
23.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and has taken treatment for 18 days as inpatient in Sankalpa Hospital, Tirupati, DBR & SK Super Speciality Hospital Tirupati.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of four months as complete laid down period.

Hence taking into consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation this court takes the loss of income during laid down period as Rs.15,500/- p.m. for 4 months.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.62,000/- (Rs.15,500X4) towards loss of income during the laid down period .

24. From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment at Sankalpa Hospital, Tirupati, DBR & SK Super Speciality Hospital Tirupati and Aster Narayanadri Hospital.

entities.text: DBR & SK Super Speciality Hospital Tirupati
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Further for 18 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.
He has taken nourishment and needs further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.
Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.40,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2022.
26. The petitioner has contended that he is aged about 74 years as on the date of accident.
Petitioner has produced Ex.P7/Aadhaar card of the petitioner which shows his date of birth as 01-01-1948 that means he was aged about 74 years.
Hence considering the Notarized copy of the Aadhaar card this court has taken the age of petitioner as 74 years.

27. So taking in to consideration the monthly income of the petitioner having considered by this tribunal as Rs.15,500/- p.m. and by considering the evidence of PW.2 he has assessed disability on Subramanyam.V vs Balakrishna on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57425363/

6 higher side, this court inclines to take the disability on whole body at 20% and when the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 74 years, as per Sarla Varma's case the multiplier applicable to the age group of above 65 is '5'.
So by applying the multiplier '5' the future loss of income due to disability comes to Rs.1,86,000/- (i.e., 15,500 x20% x 5 x12 )-.
Hence this Tribunal holds that the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,86,000/- towards future loss of income due to disability.

28. So far as future medical expense is concerned, even though PW.2 has deposed that the petitioner needs surgery for achieving union which would cost around Rs.1,00,000/- in private set up, but admittedly PW.2 has not given estimation.
Hence, this court awards compensation under the head future medical expenses to the tune of Rs.30,000/-.
29. The petitioner at his age of 74 years has suffered grievous injuries.
Hence taking in to consideration the said aspect the petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.50,000- towards loss of amenities and discomforts.

The Petitioner is entitled compensation under the following heads:
Sl.

No Heads Amount Rs.
1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 70,000/-
2. Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 40,000/-
 charges and nourishing food 3. Towards loss of income during Rs. 62,000/-
 laid up period 4.

Medical expenses Rs.2,51,596/-
5.

Future loss of income Rs.1,86,000/-
6.

Future medical expenses Rs. 30,000/-
7. Loss of amenities, discomfort and Rs. 50,000/-
disfiguration.

Therefore, this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.6,89,596/- (Rupees Six Lakh Eighty Nine Thousand Five Hundred Ninety Six only)
30.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no 2 this court directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered.
31. Issue No.3:

In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.

7
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.6,89,596/- + cost of Rs.1,500/- imposed vide order on IA No.III.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.6,91,096/- (Rupees Six Lakh Ninety One Thousand Ninety Six only).

After deducting cost of Rs 1500/- and future medical expenses to the tune of Rs.30,000/- balance sum of Rs.6,59,596/- shall carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the said amount and interest, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioner through E- payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
